newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Monday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Monday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Monday:

Spokesman Nikolaus van der Pas said Commission President Jacques Santer had reacted to statements by Jose Happart, Member of the European Parliament and the inquiry committee on Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE), who questioned the impartiality of three Commission officials during a television broadcast on Saturday. Van der Pas said Happart's declarations were unwarranted suppositions based only on the officials' nationality and said the Commission would suggest his removal from the inquiry committee.

In answer to a question, Van der Pas said the Commission would discuss relations with Ukraine, notably the question of the Chernobyl nuclear power plant, in the context of the G7 during its Wednesday meeting.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/96/961: Support for cultural cooperation projects in the European Community kaleidoscope programme.
- IP/96/962: BSE: the European Commission reacts to attacks by Mr Happart.
- IP/96/964: The Commission clears the proposed acquisition by Norsk Hydro of the remaining part of Enichem Agricoltura's fertilizer business.
- IP/96/965: EU and Korea have today signed the first Framework Agreement.
- IP/96/966: High level consultations on the environment between the European Commission and the government of Canada.
